stem: Which technique should a client use when instilling prescribed eye drops?

options.A: Touch the bottle tip to the cornea so the medication is delivered directly to the ocular surface and cannot miss the intended site.
options.B: Place the medication on the closed eyelid and wait for it to enter the conjunctival space when the eye is opened.
options.C: Pull the lower eyelid down to create a pocket, instill the prescribed drops into that pocket, and keep the bottle tip from touching the eye or eyelid.
options.D: Rub the closed eye vigorously after each drop because friction improves ocular absorption and decreases contamination of the bottle tip.

rationale: The National Eye Institute instructs patients to pull the lower eyelid down to create a pocket, hold the bottle tip just above the pocket, and squeeze the prescribed drops into it. To prevent contamination, the bottle tip should not touch the eye, eyelid, or hands. C is correct.
educational_objective: Demonstrate safe eye-drop instillation by placing drops into the lower conjunctival pocket without touching the bottle tip to the eye or eyelid.
source_document_title: How to Put in Eye Drops
source_locator: Use eye drops correctly, steps 2–4: pull lower eyelid down to make a pocket, hold tip just above pocket, instill prescribed drops. Prevent infections: do not let bottle tip touch eye or eyelid.
source_claim_supported: Prescribed eye drops should be instilled into the lower-eyelid pocket while preventing contact between the bottle tip and the eye or eyelid.

audit_findings.exact_locator: NEI Use eye drops correctly and Prevent infections sections; NCSBN Pharmacological p.12 screenshot verified
audit_findings.claim_audit: Final item directly reflects the lower-pocket and no-tip-contact instructions.

distractor_audit.A: Incorrect because the bottle tip should not touch the eye/cornea.
distractor_audit.B: Incorrect because drops are placed into the lower-eyelid pocket rather than on a closed lid.
distractor_audit.D: Incorrect because vigorous rubbing is not the recommended technique and does not reduce contamination risk.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only C satisfies both placement and contamination-prevention requirements.
audit_findings.cueing: All alternatives describe administration technique with comparable detail.
